mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior quarter is interpreted by markets as a signal of tightening financial conditions, which compresses equity discount rates and reduces expected future cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25 percentage points over the past quarter
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 60-day rolling mean during the identified tightening phase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates a labor market momentum that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.5 percentage points
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with the combined labor momentum signal (Pearson IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 3% suggests robust consumer demand that outpaces supply, leading to higher future earnings expectations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive 5-day windows, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed within the same month by a decline in inventory levels (implied via supply chain stress) indicates supply-side weakness that reduces market confidence and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by at least 5% in a month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the 60-day rolling average during the identified supply contraction (Mann-Whitney U p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2% for two consecutive months while the federal funds rate remains below 3%, it signals a shift toward price stability concerns that prompts a flight to quality and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 2% for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 3%
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 60-day historical mean during such inflation-rate conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% followed by a sustained rise in labor force participation (implied by PAYEMS) suggests a demographic or policy-driven expansion in the working-age population, which boosts equity valuations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months while PAYEMS increases by 5% or more over the same period
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the combined labor force expansion signal (Spearman IC < 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in residential investment (implied proxy via HOUST) over three consecutive months indicates cooling real estate demand, which reduces overall economic momentum and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by at least 8% over three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the 60-day rolling average during the identified cooling period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and supply chain activity (implied via RSAFS) both show simultaneous double-digit declines in the same month, it signals a systemic supply disruption that dampens investor sentiment and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >10% in a month AND RSAFS decreases by >10% in the same month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 180-day historical mean during such dual-industry declines (Mann-Whitney U p > 0.05).
